About AI discoveries in 2026

This selection contains 613 catalog entries dated 2 Jan 2026 to 19 Nov 2026. 612 include structured evidence annotations describing reported tests, the AI contribution and remaining limits. Missing annotations mean those details have not been structured here, not that a study lacks evidence.

Dates follow the catalog publication policy. Coverage is selected and incomplete; entries can overlap or describe several results. Counts do not measure independent discoveries, clinical benefit or worldwide research output. Read the selection and evidence policy or compare catalog coverage by year and field.

19 Nov 2026Fabrice Baudoin

GPT-6.1 Astra assists a gradient rank theorem for metric measure spaces

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: Fabrice Baudoin develops a finite-rank gradient framework and proves that the pointwise gradient rank is strictly below p almost everywhere under the hypotheses of his rank theorem. The result assumes a small-scale doubling measure, a Poincaré inequality and cutoffs with a matching energy scale above the exponent p.

Technology: GPT-6.1 Astra; GPT-6.1 Sol

19 Nov 2026Stanford University

Calibrated AI detectors estimate rising AI-assisted drafting in four state courts

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: Stanford researchers applied the learned EditLens detector with ScoreMix calibration to 127,518 complaints from four U.S. county court systems. Their selected settings estimated rising AI-like drafting, reaching about 38% in Santa Clara and 36% in San Francisco in 2026 for non-debt-collection complaints. Calibration used documented hallucination filings and assumed their detector-score distribution represented other AI-assisted writing. Detector settings, imperfect controls, case mix and selection of conspicuous AI mistakes limit the estimates. These are population estimates, not proof that any particular filing used AI, fabricated citations or affected a judicial outcome. November 19 is the institutional announcement date; the working paper posting day is unestablished.

Technology: EditLens (Llama-3.2-3B); ScoreMix calibration

XCAPE proposes nine previously unmatched crystal structure assignments

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: In an arXiv preprint, researchers used XCAPE and the SevenNet-Omni machine learning interatomic potential to revisit existing powder X-ray diffraction patterns. QORA designs quantum control sequences that extend spin coherence in diamond

AI contribution
The learned surrogate made a high-dimensional global sensitivity decomposition tractable and localized conditional parameter effects that pooled or single-parameter summaries concealed. Those interpretations were compared with original simulator data and explicit verification runs.
Test and result
A seven-parameter SCAPS-1D dataset retained 4,396 runs, with 3,525 training and 871 separately sampled test points. The selected LightGBM model was refitted on all retained runs for 262,144-evaluation sensitivity analysis. The source attributed 17.8% of modeled efficiency variance to interactions. Thickness and acceptor doping had near-zero first-order sensitivity but nonzero total effects; stratified original simulator data showed sign reversals. Separate simulator verification exposed wrong donor-density trends and overoptimistic ranking of the surrogate-selected optimum.

Results depend on the chosen simulator, layer stack, sampled ranges and numerical assumptions. Known defect-density effects were recovered rather than established as new physics. Surrogate sensitivity shares are not measured device variance, and original simulator checks are not external experimental replication. 6 Nov 2026The University of Tokyo; National Astronomical Observatory of Japan; Tohoku University; Subaru Telescope

PCFNet-guided spectroscopy confirms four protoclusters at redshift 3.3–3.4

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: Subaru/MOIRCS spectroscopy of four PCFNet-selected candidate regions confirmed four protoclusters at z = 3.316, 3.403, 3.408 and 3.425, across three regions, with galaxy-density peaks more than five times the uniform distribution. Twenty-three spectroscopically identified members are largely on the star-forming main sequence. Model-weighted estimates put star-formation-rate density above cosmic averages, while metallicity differences are marginal in two systems and consistent with the field in the others.

Technology: PCFNet point-cloud deep-learning protocluster finder

Editorial relevance 60 physics Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
PCFNet used broad-band optical photometry and galaxy positions to assign protocluster-membership probabilities and identify candidate regions. The model outputs determined which regions received Subaru/MOIRCS follow-up and prioritized slit targets; their probabilities also informed member selection and the authors’ volume/SFR-density estimator. Spectroscopy then tested those predictions, finding a 40% member detection rate among high-probability galaxies and confirming three of four observed regions.
Test and result
Subaru/MOIRCS spectroscopy of four PCFNet-selected candidate regions confirmed four protoclusters at z = 3.316, 3.403, 3.408 and 3.425, across three regions, with galaxy-density peaks more than five times the uniform distribution.
Limitation / still unknown
This is a small follow-up sample: four of 121 PCFNet candidates were targeted, and the parent catalogue is trained on simulated galaxies. Four protoclusters are confirmed across three of four observed regions; a fourth observed candidate region had no significant redshift peak. One of the confirmed regions had previously been reported as a photometric candidate, so this is a spectroscopic confirmation/characterization result rather than four wholly unprecedented structures. The halo masses are inferred from member stellar masses, not direct lensing measurements. The elevated SFR densities depend on membership-probability weighting and are sensitive to assumed geometry, volume and methodology. Metallicity excesses are only 1.4–2 sigma in two systems; two others are statistically consistent with the field. The authors’ proposed gas-inflow/recycling explanation is interpretive.

Retrospective eight-site study of 83 patients with clinical MRI and longitudinal neurological assessments. Editorial relevance 47 physics Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
CoSR progressively searched for interpretable dimensionless groups and combined their relationships instead of fitting one end-to-end expression. Applied to hypersonic simulation data, it identified a dominant angle-of-attack/Mach term and a Reynolds-number-dependent viscous correction, then fitted geometry-specific constants for two body shapes. Earlier canonical-law and fluid examples in the same paper are framework validations and are not counted separately here.
Test and result
A Chain of Symbolic Regression (CoSR) analysis of hypersonic simulation data derived an interpretable non-power-product scaling relation for axial-force coefficient across sharp-cone and blunt-body configurations.
Limitation / still unknown
The aerodynamic relation was inferred from hypersonic simulation data for two configurations (sharp cone and blunt body), not independently measured flight or wind-tunnel data. It is a parameterized model over the analyzed configuration/data range; external validation and broader geometry coverage are not established in the source. The simpler dominant component is linked to known hypersonic invariance, while the learned viscous correction and geometry-specific scaling provide the paper’s new modeled relationship. Do not treat the authors’ drag-component interpretations as direct measurements.

Finding: Ten learned classifiers tested whether leukocyte-associated RNA retention affects platelet RNA cancer detection. In a matched 754-sample analysis, training on high-retention samples modestly improved some classifiers; most differences were not significant. Adding the retention score to a full-cohort classifier changed AUC only from 0.9247 to 0.9249, challenging a blanket assumption that this signal should always be removed.

Technology: SVM; LightGBM; XGBoost; random forest and other learned classifiers

Editorial relevance 40 medicine Original source Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
Learned classifiers provided the cancer-detection experiments needed to quantify how differing RNA-retention strata change diagnostic performance; the finding concerns assay signal composition rather than a new general classifier architecture.
Test and result
Analysis combined 2,351 public platelet RNA samples with a marker panel derived from single-cell data from 29 donors. Matching yielded 377 high-retention and 377 low-retention samples, with cancer type balanced but residual collection-center imbalance. Ten classifiers used separate training/validation/test sets across repeated splits and validation-only hyperparameter optimization. SVM mean test AUC was 0.76 when trained on low-retention versus 0.84 on high-retention samples; corresponding LightGBM values were 0.74/0.79 and XGBoost 0.71/0.74. Most other training-retention comparisons were not significant.
Limitation / still unknown
RNA retention score is a compositional proxy, not physical purity or a causal manipulation. Residual collection-center confounding remains; repeated overlapping splits do not provide 30 independent biological replications. Model-specific modest effects do not establish universally beneficial retention, a correction standard or clinical benefit. The full-cohort added-score comparison was nearly null, and generalization to separately collected clinical cohorts is untested.

Technology: DBSCAN unsupervised density-based clustering

Editorial relevance 33 medicine Original source Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
DBSCAN learned density structure in longitudinal QA changes and flagged sparse observations, enabling targeted linkage of unusual measured signals to service documentation rather than a fixed list of expected calibration effects.
Test and result
Retrospective 2018–2024 EPID QA measurements and service histories from nine TrueBeam accelerators across six institutions. DBSCAN fit dense/noise groups separately to one-dimensional changes in each machine/metric, with a dataset-specific neighborhood rule. In one machine, 15 jaw-position outliers included a 1.3 mm apparent shift near a documented calibration. Independently paired ion-chamber measurements supported selected output-change comparisons on only two machines/12 events, not all DBSCAN flags.
Limitation / still unknown
Temporal associations do not establish service causation or independently confirmed physical faults. Apparent jaw shifts after steering may be measurement artifacts. Acquisition timing and detector recalibration records were incomplete, and two machines lacked complete service histories. Clustering parameters were not optimized against prospective truth; noise-versus-cluster statistical comparisons are circular. No sensitivity/specificity, superiority to existing QA, safer treatment or patient benefit was established.

Test and result
Twenty-nine patient plans were split by patient/plan into 23 development and six held-out test plans. GroupKFold tuning and development-only feature selection preceded final fitting. Against delivered-position machine logs, test MAE was 0.054 mm and RMSE 0.144 mm. Nine further patients supplied independent plans over six fractions; predicted and logged leaf positions were separately inserted into plans for dose recalculation on patient CTs. Agreement concerns reconstructed dose distributions, not in-vivo measured dose.
Limitation / still unknown
Single treatment center and accelerator; many leaf/control-point observations derive from few patients. Machine logs are the position reference and both dose distributions use the same dose-calculation system, so no independent physical dosimetry or outcome benefit is established. Dosimetric deviations were small and gamma agreement already high for delivered plans; the study does not establish detection of clinically dangerous failures or safer treatment.

27 Oct 2026Infinite Ascent

Paper trading agents echoed peer wording without a detectable immediate trade shift

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: In a seven-day paper trading study with 200 agents across four model families, later-starting board agents reused peers' phrases 6.8 percentage points more often when they could see a fresh post. A timing-based comparison found no detectable same-morning shift in matching trades, with an estimate of 2.4 points and a 95% interval of −4.1 to 9.3.

Technology: Opus 5.5; GPT-6.1 Sol; Grok 4.6; DeepSeek V4 Pro

Family GPT-6: profile · models page

Editorial relevance 40 computer science Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Preprint · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
Four learned model families ran separate paper trading accounts and produced peer messages while retaining independent decisions. Frozen views and time-stamped paper orders made phrase and order comparisons possible.
Test and result
Timing-based comparisons found 6.8 percentage points more same-morning eight-word phrase reuse for pairs with an opportunity to read a recent peer post (95% interval 1.7–11.8, 68 board group mornings). In a separate comparison subtracting timing differences in isolated groups, same-direction orders in the same stock differed by 2.4 points (95% interval −4.1 to 9.3).
Limitation / still unknown
The study used one group per communication regime and model family, with only seven trading days and simulated fills at live prices. Timing was not randomized. The interval leaves room for some short-run effects and says nothing about market impact.

Technology: Ridge regression of simulated light-curve statistics

Publication: Preprint · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
Fitted ridge regression maps simulated multiband light-curve statistics to logarithmic half-light radii. Models trained under simplified assumptions were applied to a separately partitioned target with independent lens motions and a lens mass distribution.
Test and result
Joint fits for three quadruply lensed quasar configurations and populations of 128 matched quads underestimated radii by 27.8%, 20.9% and 5.6% when training omitted relative motions. Matched-physics controls showed median biases between −0.003 and −0.001 dex.

The experiment simulated three fixed lens and disk configurations. It omitted survey selection, photometric noise, observing gaps and intrinsic variability, so the offsets are not corrections established for observed quasars.

Learned simulations mapped a shallow free-energy landscape for acridine

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: Anharmonic simulations using a fine-tuned MACE potential placed four metastable acridine forms 2.27–2.83 kJ/mol above Form II at 300 K. In the simulations, Form VIII became the most stable member of that group at higher temperature. Laboratory transitions partly agreed with the predicted changes in ordering.

Technology: MolCryst fine-tuned MACE-MH1 interatomic potential

Editorial relevance 47 materials Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Preprint · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
A MACE-MH1 interatomic model fine-tuned on electronic-structure configurations supplied energies and forces for anharmonic thermodynamic integration.
Test and result
At 300 K the estimated Gibbs free energies of four metastable acridine forms were 2.27–2.83 kJ/mol above Form II. Form VIII was estimated to become the most stable member of that metastable group at higher temperature. Observed transitions partly agreed with the predicted crossovers.
Limitation / still unknown
The absolute free-energy differences are computational estimates. The comparison is with observed phase transformations, and Form IV was omitted from the anharmonic calculation. The main text discusses a value near 350 K, while the supporting protocol lists temperature propagation over 280–340 K; that endpoint is not promoted here. Laboratory transitions only partly match: the calculation leaves Form III more stable throughout, unlike the observed Form VIII–III crossover.

25 Oct 2026Washington University in St. Louis

Latent transition learning maps short-term changes in Parkinson clinical profiles

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: A probabilistically learned latent-transition model followed 250 people with Parkinson disease across two clinical assessments about 2.5 years apart. Most retained their model-defined profile, while a fourth severe multidomain profile emerged at follow-up and included a high proportion with dementia. These are observational clinical groupings and transitions, without established biological subtypes or lifetime convergence trajectories.

Technology: Latent class mixture learning; latent transition analysis in Mplus

Editorial relevance 40 medicine Original source Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
Probabilistic latent-mixture and transition learning estimated multidomain classes and membership transitions from clinical measurements; these learned representations enabled the reported stability and emergent severe-profile finding. Conventional secondary logistic regression is not the enabling AI claim.
Test and result
Eleven motor, cognitive and psychiatric indicators defined learned latent classes. Mplus latent-transition models compared three- and four-class follow-up structures using likelihood-based fit, information criteria and entropy; the selected model had three baseline and four follow-up classes. Among 250 analytic participants, 190 retained their class over a mean 2.51 years. The severe multidomain follow-up class had dementia in 64%, versus at most 7% in the other classes. Available autopsy information supported exclusion of nine non-Parkinson diagnoses before the analytic cohort was formed.
Limitation / still unknown
Only two assessment times and a predominantly White, non-Hispanic cohort constrain trajectory interpretation. Classes are data-dependent clinical profiles, not validated biological taxonomy. Dementia-related indicators contribute to the learned profiles, so dementia enrichment is not independent diagnostic validation. Same-cohort class transitions and secondary regression associations do not establish causal progression, universal eventual convergence, independent forecasting or treatment benefit.

Editorial relevance 40 humanities Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

AI contribution
An energy-based neural policy learned from student demonstration occupancy selects presentation modes and overrides conflicting choices during new classroom use; measured learning and choice patterns are the represented field result. Test and result
StuEDM was trained on 244 earlier student trajectories; StuCQL used 2,716. The Spring 2026 live study had 104 completers. Removing perfect-pretest students left 26 StuEDM and 27 StuCQL students; the random-mode Expert comparator was augmented with 11 prior-semester students. Limitation / still unknown
The Expert arm is partly historical, and non-significant baseline tests do not prove population equivalence. Other direct learning comparisons against StuCQL were not significant. Multiple directional outcomes, ceiling exclusions, a single course and small samples limit inference. Override counts include repeated decisions within students; decision-level significance is not independent-person replication. Longer tutor time is measured engagement, not proof of benefit. Earlier dissertation chapters reproduce published methods, which are not represented as new here; October 20 is the located arXiv version date, not a claim of absolute first circulation.

5 Oct 2026The University of Tokyo; Los Alamos National Laboratory

Recurrent neural network reveals near-critical seeding of topological defects in Kibble–Zurek simulations

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: In numerical simulations of a one-dimensional Landau–Ginzburg phase transition, a recurrent neural network predicted the final locations of topological defects from short sequences of order-parameter fluctuations during the Kibble–Zurek impulse regime, before freeze-out and before the defects were macroscopically visible. Prediction error across quench rates followed power-law scaling consistent with the Kibble–Zurek freeze-out time, indicating that information about the eventual defect pattern is encoded in near-critical fluctuations in this model.

Technology: Recurrent neural network (RNN); LSTM and Transformer architectures were also checked

Editorial relevance 47 physics Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The RNN analyzed short time sequences from numerical order-parameter dynamics and inferred the final kink count and positions from small fluctuations during the impulse regime. This allowed the authors to identify when information about future defect positions becomes predictable, a quantity not directly provided by conventional Kibble–Zurek defect-density scaling. They report similar prediction behavior with LSTM and Transformer models, suggesting the result is not specific to one architecture.
Test and result
In numerical simulations of a one-dimensional Landau–Ginzburg phase transition, a recurrent neural network predicted the final locations of topological defects from short sequences of order-parameter fluctuations during the Kibble–Zurek impulse regime, before freeze-out and before the defects were macroscopically visible.
Limitation / still unknown
This is a computational result from a noisy one-dimensional Landau–Ginzburg model, not an experimental observation of defects in a material or cosmological system. The paper uses overdamped dynamics (η=1), low noise temperature θ=10⁻⁸, a finite periodic grid and simulated training/test samples; similar behavior at another noise setting is reported in supplementary material. The finding is consistent with the Kibble–Zurek mechanism and an earlier deconstruction of its dynamics; it does not establish that this prediction method applies unchanged to all phase transitions. The PRL article was published 2026-10-05; the original arXiv preprint was submitted 2025-08-28 and revised as v2 on 2026-09-10.

4 Oct 2026Microsoft Research; independent research collaboration

AI-assisted proof establishes a dimension-independent KLS isoperimetric bound

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: Zhao Song and Xinzhi Zhang prove a universal, dimension-independent bound for the Kannan–Lovász–Simonovits constant of isotropic log-concave probability measures, resolving the KLS conjecture. Their proof repeatedly refines bounds on polynomial variance and curvature; the authors report that AI tools helped explore more than 100 approaches, obtain the earlier log-star bound, and develop and verify the final proof. Independent researchers also posted proofs, and the paper’s streamlined proof is being formalized in Lean. The 1 October preprint gave a slowly dimension-dependent bound; the 4 October version established the dimension-independent theorem described here.

31 Aug 2026Brookhaven National Laboratory

GPT-5.6 helps prove an exact mapping between frustrated and field-driven spin chains

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: A single-author preprint proves that every finite one-dimensional open O(n) spin chain with arbitrary inhomogeneous nearest- and next-nearest-neighbor interactions has an exact, temperature-independent Hamiltonian mapping to a simpler nearest-neighbor chain with axial single-spin potentials. A parallel result for q-state Potts chains yields a closed-form solution for every q ≥ 2 and finite chain length. The theorem generalizes a 1990 Heisenberg-chain challenge and connects spontaneous collective behavior from competing interactions to field-induced behavior.

Researchers trained convolutional neural networks on E11.5 mouse heart, limb and midbrain chromatin-accessibility data, then fine-tuned the models using validated human and mouse enhancers and used model-guided sequence optimization to design 15 synthetic enhancers.
Limitation / still unknown
The functional test was a transgenic reporter assay at embryonic day 11.5, not editing or activation of an endogenous native gene locus. Fifteen selected sequences were tested (five per target), so the reported all-positive result does not estimate success across every generated candidate. Some designs had weaker off-target activity, particularly in related mesenchymal tissues. These results do not establish therapeutic efficacy or safe gene therapy.

Editorial relevance 60 materials Original source Suggest a correction

AI contribution
The MLIP relaxed approximately 1,000-atom disordered supercells and estimated mixing enthalpy and atom-energy-distribution descriptors for the 462-composition search. Limitation / still unknown
This is an unrefereed arXiv preprint. Only three of 16 tested compositions formed phase-pure corundum high-entropy oxides; most attempts produced competing phases, and rhodium-containing samples showed redox instability. Synthesis outcomes depended strongly on route: the three corundum HEOs were phase-pure only with one of solid-state or combustion synthesis. The ordered oxide’s structure is supported by powder diffraction/Rietveld refinement, but exact site preferences could not be conclusively determined from pXRD. The screening supports candidate ranking, not reliable prediction of phase purity or synthesis conditions for arbitrary HEOs.

Follow-up experiments found that pharmacological or genetic Chk2 inhibition rescued dopaminergic-neuron loss and motor deficits in PD mouse models, supporting CHK2 as a disease-associated mediator in the tested systems.
Limitation / still unknown
The neuroprotective evidence is from experimental Parkinson’s disease models and mice, not human patients or clinical efficacy. XunZi also nominated IRAK4, but the abstract specifically reports Chk2 inhibition rescue; do not imply equivalent causal validation for every AI-nominated target. The Nature article’s complete indexed text was read; direct open may be blocked by a cookie redirect.

4 Aug 2026ATLAS Collaboration; CERN

Boosted decision tree enables first observation of two simultaneously longitudinally polarized Z bosons

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: Using 164 fb⁻¹ of 13.6 TeV proton–proton data and a statistical combination with the Run 2 measurement, ATLAS reports the first observation of ZZ production with both Z bosons longitudinally polarized, at 6.5σ observed (5.6σ expected). The combined signal strength is 1.22 ± 0.21; the Run 3 measurement also reports polarization fractions across the fiducial phase space and two four-lepton invariant-mass ranges, consistent with Standard Model predictions.

Technology: Boosted decision tree (BDT) classifier

Editorial relevance 60 physics Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Preprint · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The BDT is trained on polarization-sensitive lepton angular observables to separate longitudinal-longitudinal ZZ events from transverse or mixed-polarization events. Its score distribution is the fitted observable used to extract the signal strength and significance.
Test and result
Using 164 fb⁻¹ of 13.6 TeV proton–proton data and a statistical combination with the Run 2 measurement, ATLAS reports the first observation of ZZ production with both Z bosons longitudinally polarized, at 6.5σ observed (5.6σ expected).
Limitation / still unknown
The ATLAS paper was submitted to PRL as a preprint on 2026-07-14; the cited official ATLAS briefing is dated 2026-08-04. The 6.5σ first observation combines the Run 3 analysis with the prior Run 2 measurement, whose standalone significance was 4.3σ. The Run 3 analysis alone reports 5.1σ. The measured fractions agree with the Standard Model; the statistical uncertainty dominates and polarization-template modeling is the leading systematic uncertainty. This is an experimental observation from ATLAS data, not evidence of physics beyond the Standard Model.

Deep-learning splice prediction links a PARP2 variant to altered protein isoforms and influenza susceptibility

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: By combining single-cell splicing-QTL analysis during influenza A infection with SpliceAI/Pangolin annotation and statistical fine-mapping, researchers prioritized causal splice variants. They experimentally characterized rs2297616 in PARP2: its A allele creates an alternative 5′ splice donor, adding 39 nucleotides and producing a protein isoform 13 amino acids longer. CRISPR-edited A549 cells showed the predicted splice and protein changes; the A-allele edited cells also had higher influenza A infection than G-allele cells. Editorial relevance 60 biology Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
Deep-learning splice models prioritized variants predicted to alter donor/acceptor sites; statistical fine-mapping and sQTL association narrowed causal candidates. The AI-supported analysis nominated rs2297616; the authors then tested its splice and protein-isoform effects using reporter assays, CRISPR-edited A549 cells, sequencing and western blotting, and assessed influenza infection in edited cells.
Test and result
They experimentally characterized rs2297616 in PARP2: its A allele creates an alternative 5′ splice donor, adding 39 nucleotides and producing a protein isoform 13 amino acids longer.
Limitation / still unknown
The 96-donor LCL association is observational and modest (the paper reports p=0.029 for the genotype association). Infection experiments used edited A549 lung epithelial cells, not patients or an in-vivo infection model. The same locus had been linked to alternative splicing previously, but the paper provides new evidence connecting genotype to PARP2 protein isoform expression and to influenza susceptibility. Broader viral-susceptibility implications remain unproven.

AI contribution
The CNN detected SZ cluster candidates in combined ACT+Planck maps, creating the candidate catalogue analyzed here. The ComPACT catalogue contains 2,962 SZ-selected candidates; the paper confirms approximately 60% as clusters, so the full candidate list must not be treated as confirmed. AI contribution
After the unbiased genome-wide CRISPR screen, VirtualCRISPR scored whether perturbing each gene in primary adult keratinocytes would alter IL17RA expression. The authors combined screen enrichment with the model’s lower prior probability for noncanonical hits to prioritize high-novelty regulators; targeted CRISPR knockout and pharmacologic mouse experiments tested the resulting biology.
Test and result
A genome-wide CRISPR knockout screen in primary human epidermal keratinocytes, combined with VirtualCRISPR language-model prioritization, identified ALOX5 and OXTR as previously underappreciated cell-intrinsic regulators of surface IL17RA.

The genetic validation used primary cells from two donors, while therapeutic effects were tested in an imiquimod-induced mouse model, not patients. Learned constitutive fitting identifies a composition–age tradeoff in hydrogel mechanics

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: Gaussian-process-guided optimization fitted constitutive coefficients to measured hydrogel stress–strain curves. The resulting analysis identified a compensatory relationship between fibrin concentration and matrix-source age at low to moderate strain, alongside coefficient-specific effects that did not extend uniformly to high strain. These are model-based interpretations of tested materials, without independent validation of newly designed formulations or demonstrated cellular effects.

Technology: Gaussian-process surrogate Bayesian optimization with expected improvement for constitutive coefficient fitting

Editorial relevance 33 materials Original source Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The learned Gaussian-process surrogate adaptively searched constitutive parameters against measured curves, enabling coefficient-level composition analysis and the represented mechanical tradeoff beyond reporting optimizer convergence alone.
Test and result
Experimental rheology curves from basal-membrane and fibrin/matrix hydrogel formulations were fitted with a second-order polynomial hyperelastic model. A Gaussian-process surrogate learned fit error across coefficient settings and expected improvement selected subsequent finite-element evaluations. Statistical analysis of fitted coefficients supported a concentration/source-age compensation at low to moderate strain; the higher-strain coefficient effects were not statistically established.
Limitation / still unknown
Fit error is agreement to the same experimental curves, not held-out prediction. Constitutive assumptions, coefficient dependence and small replicate sets constrain mechanistic interpretation. Variability intervals were adjusted for physical plausibility rather than uniformly calibrated predictive coverage. Some compositional trends recover prior literature; the admitted result is the specific combined tradeoff, not first discovery that concentration or age affects stiffness. New formulations, cell behavior, tissue function and in-vivo benefit were not independently tested.

The 2019–2023 cohort comprised 367 Xuhui-campus cases split into 254 training and 113 internal-validation patients, plus 51 Pudong-campus and 20 Northern-Jiangsu validation patients. Clinical vignettes and comparison with later-available kinetic biomarkers do not demonstrate prospective clinical utility.

Product profiles differed between cell-free extracts and yeast; these results do not establish universal performance across enzymes or production settings.

Editorial relevance 47 medicine Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

AI contribution
Researchers used five feature-selection algorithms to identify shared predictors and trained/evaluated eight classifiers on routine clinical and laboratory measurements. This is retrospective diagnostic validation, not evidence that screening with the model improves health outcomes or shortens diagnosis in practice. All participants had been referred for immunofixation testing at tertiary or regional hospitals; an unselected community or primary-care population was not studied. The 627-patient later cohort was time-extended but not strictly prospective. The model is an adjunct for flagging patients for confirmatory tests; immunofixation remained the reference standard, and the paper states broader population validation and clinical utility remain to be established.

The source measured fifteen early-onset tumors, fifteen later-onset tumors and fifteen adjacent-normal tissue specimens. Editorial relevance 60 chemistry Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The authors trained predictive models on phenotypic screening data from >11,000 compounds, then used their scores as rewards/objectives in a generative workflow to propose molecules intended to kill one pancreatic-cancer cell line while sparing another or control cells. Candidate molecules or close purchasable analogues were experimentally tested and dose-response validated.
Test and result
The IRB Barcelona team trained cell-line cytotoxicity predictors on data from more than 11,000 compounds assayed across pancreatic-cancer and control cell lines, then integrated the models with a reinforcement-learning generative system to design molecules for cell-selective effects.
Limitation / still unknown
This is a proof-of-concept hit-discovery study using in-vitro cell-line assays, not evidence of tumor selectivity in patients or an animal efficacy result. Only binary cytotoxicity labels at 10 μM informed the predictors; 45 generated structures or close analogues were tested, with 20 showing desired phenotypes and 18 confirming in dose-response assays. Exact generated structures were not always the synthesized compounds, and measured IC50 spans 0.97–16.6 μM for 12 of the confirmed hits. The paper explicitly characterizes this as an early hit-discovery stage.

12 May 2026ETH Zurich; Weizmann Institute of Science; University Children’s Hospital Zurich and University of Zurich

Machine-learning metabolomics identifies widespread promiscuous activities in Escherichia coli enzymes

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: In vitro metabolomics of 667 purified E. coli enzymes, analyzed with a machine-learning-derived multivariate classifier, indicated previously unrecognized promiscuous activities in 11% of enzymes tested. Follow-up reconstruction assigned 22 reaction stoichiometries to 11 enzymes, with four reactions experimentally validated; examples include expanded nucleotide-substrate use by DeoA, cofactor and sugar promiscuity in NanK, and FMN dephosphorylation by CobC. Follow-up assays also found that pyrimidine-specific ribonucleoside hydrolase RihB acted on thymidine, guanosine and deoxyuridine, further extending its measured substrate range.

Editorial relevance 60 biology Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
A machine-learning-derived multivariate classifier, with a reported false-discovery rate of 33%, detected unexpected changes in metabolite ion traces in the enzyme assays and helped nominate candidate promiscuous activities. The researchers then reconstructed candidate reaction stoichiometries and experimentally validated four reactions.
Test and result
In vitro metabolomics of 667 purified E. coli enzymes, analyzed with a machine-learning-derived multivariate classifier, indicated previously unrecognized promiscuous activities in 11% of enzymes tested.
Limitation / still unknown
The classifier operated at a 33% false-discovery rate; the 135 ion traces were putatively annotated, and only four of 22 reconstructed reaction stoichiometries were experimentally validated. Therefore the full 11% result is a set of candidate activities, not 11% independently confirmed enzyme functions. The RihB activities were prompted by a low-confidence potassium-thymidine-adduct trace and then tested directly with purified enzyme; they should be distinguished from the classifier’s higher-confidence hit set.

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: An interpretable machine-learning and active-learning workflow screened a virtual library of 18,264 candidate passivation molecules and guided synthesis/testing of selected candidates for perovskite solar cells. The newly identified molecule 5-(aminomethyl)nicotinonitrile hydroiodide (5ANI) yielded 0.05 cm² devices at 27.22% power-conversion efficiency (27.18% certified) and 21.4 cm² mini-modules at 23.49%. Under the reported ISOS-L-1I operating test, 5ANI devices retained 98.7% of initial efficiency after 1,200 hours.

Technology: SISSO interpretable symbolic regression and NGBoost active-learning models, coupled to DFT calculations and a Bayesian-optimization/symbolic-regression automated fabrication platform

Editorial relevance 60 materials Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The team used DFT descriptors and SISSO regression trained on measurements from 20 known passivator/device sets to learn structure–performance relationships. NGBoost active learning reduced the computational cost of estimating interfacial properties across an 18,264-molecule virtual library; model-guided screening selected four candidates for synthesis and experimental validation. 5ANI emerged as a passivator for which the automated device-fabrication loop optimized deposition and processing settings. The ML models guided material choice, while the closed-loop platform refined device fabrication and generated measured feedback.
Test and result
An interpretable machine-learning and active-learning workflow screened a virtual library of 18,264 candidate passivation molecules and guided synthesis/testing of selected candidates for perovskite solar cells.
Limitation / still unknown
This is a result for a specific perovskite composition, cell architecture and passivation/fabrication protocol. The ML regression was trained on only 20 initial known passivator/device datasets; four selected candidates were experimentally synthesized/validated. The reported champion efficiency is a small-area cell result; the mini-module efficiency is lower (23.49%) and laboratory-scale. The 1,200-hour stability result follows the stated ISOS-L-1I protocol and does not establish commercial lifetime. The paper reports high reproducibility from its automated setup, not factory-scale manufacturing. This is a different study and molecule from the 2024 Bayesian-optimized hole-transport materials record (Science DOI 10.1126/science.ads0901): here AI identifies an interfacial passivator 5ANI.

Editorial relevance 33 biology Original source Suggest a correction

AI contribution
The learned RF/LASSO intersection reduced measured expression candidates for subsequent tissue-reference and outcome comparisons, enabling the represented marker prioritization. Generic pathway analysis or pseudotime alone is not treated as an enabling causal finding.
Test and result
The source used 45 paired early-stage tumor/adjacent specimens in GSE32863 for differential filtering and RF/LASSO selection, yielding nine candidate markers. Expression comparisons used further public series. In GSE63459, comprising 33 tumors and 32 adjacent controls, IGSF9 expression showed reported AUC 0.903 with 95% confidence interval 0.816–0.960. Limitation / still unknown
Candidate prioritization incorporated the additional cohort results, so the final singled-out marker is not an untouched independently selected test. Paired tissues, platform differences and cohort composition may confound expression signals. Prior lung-cancer work already implicated IGSF9; no first causal-role claim is made. Pseudotime, inferred cell communication and copy-number patterns do not prove that IGSF9 causes malignant differentiation, immune escape or invasion; the source explicitly lacked functional validation.

20 Mar 2026CMS Collaboration

ParticleNet enables first hadron-collider W-boson mass measurement from hadronic decays

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: Using 138 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV proton–proton data, CMS reports the first measurement of the W-boson mass in an all-jets final state at a hadron collider: 80.83 ± 0.55 GeV. The result comes from unfolded groomed jet-mass distributions for boosted hadronic W+jets events. The mass-decorrelated ParticleNet graph neural network tagger provides the main result by selecting the W-jet sample and suppressing quark/gluon multijet background; a non-neural N₂ tagger is used as a cross-check.

Technology: ParticleNet mass-decorrelated graph neural network jet tagger

Editorial relevance 47 physics Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The analysis uses ParticleNet as its main W-jet tagger. Its graph neural network treats jet constituents as an unordered particle cloud and classifies W→qq′ jets against QCD multijet backgrounds; its mass-decorrelated output defines the signal/control regions used for the primary measurement. The N₂ substructure observable is a separate cross-check.
Test and result
Using 138 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV proton–proton data, CMS reports the first measurement of the W-boson mass in an all-jets final state at a hadron collider: 80.83 ± 0.55 GeV.
Limitation / still unknown
This is an all-jets boosted-W extraction with 0.55 GeV total uncertainty, much less precise than the CMS leptonic-channel W-mass result; the paper frames it as a first step toward future all-jets precision measurements and as a test of jet-substructure modeling. The earlier preliminary CMS result of 80.77 ± 0.57 GeV was superseded by this same paper’s published 80.83 ± 0.55 GeV result and is not counted separately. Jet tagging, QCD background estimation, unfolding, hadronization and jet-energy modeling contribute analysis dependence and uncertainties.

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

The universal lower-bound theorem was formally checked in Lean 4.

Technology: Claude Opus 4.5 LLM agent with SageMath, Rust exhaustive solver, simulated annealing and Lean 4 verification tools

Family Claude: profile · models page

Editorial relevance 67 mathematics Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Preprint · Test context: prospective or independent check. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The agent identified an all-even row-distance parity pattern in numerical search data, formulated and helped prove the lower bound, and used model review to catch proof errors. SageMath and a Rust solver supported symbolic analysis and enumeration; simulated annealing found matching constructions through n=52. Human strategic direction supplied the decisive pivot to the minimum-positive-imbalance question. Lean 4 formally verifies the lower-bound theorem itself.
Test and result
A collaborative LLM-plus-symbolic-computation study proved that every n×n Latin square with n ≡ 1 (mod 3) has imbalance at least 4n(n−1)/9.
Limitation / still unknown
This is an arXiv preprint (v2 dated 2026-08-13), not yet peer-reviewed in the sources checked. The universal proven theorem is a lower bound for n ≡ 1 mod 3. Matching constructions, and hence demonstrated tightness, are computationally established only for n=4,7,…,52; the paper does not prove that the bound is attained for every larger order. Lean 4 formalizes the lower-bound inequality, not the finite construction search or universal tightness.

5 Mar 2026University of Birmingham; University of Cambridge

Time-delay neural networks expose three fault-development phases across laboratory pressure regimes

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: A time-delay neural network trained on multi-parameter acoustic-emission records from Alzo-granite triaxial tests at 5–40 MPa resolved three recurring phases: microcrack nucleation marked by waveform-scattering changes, fault growth with evolving spatial and magnitude distributions, and coalescence marked by peak-delay increases and b-value changes. The model also predicted stress-drop timing and size across axial-splitting and shear-localization failures. This is a laboratory result, not a natural-earthquake precursor claim.

Technology: Genetic-algorithm-optimized time-delay neural network (TDNN)

Editorial relevance 53 physics Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The TDNN integrated time-dependent acoustic-emission waveform features (peak delay, coda Q/scattering) and occurrence measures (event rate, Gutenberg–Richter b-value, spatial fractal dimension), dynamically weighting them to model stress/strain evolution and identify repeatable phases across pressure conditions. Leave-one-experiment-out validation tested cross-condition generalization.
Test and result
A time-delay neural network trained on multi-parameter acoustic-emission records from Alzo-granite triaxial tests at 5–40 MPa resolved three recurring phases: microcrack nucleation marked by waveform-scattering changes, fault growth with evolving spatial and magnitude distributions, and coalescence marked by peak-delay increases and b-value changes.
Limitation / still unknown
The analysis uses four laboratory experiments in Alzo granite, so results are sample- and apparatus-limited and do not establish natural-earthquake predictability. Training-data smoothing and the small number of experiments constrain generalization; stress estimates show more variability and modelled subtle phase transitions are less accurate. The observed phase interpretation is based on model-assisted analysis of acoustic emissions and measured mechanical data.

25 Feb 2026CMS Collaboration; CERN Large Hadron Collider

First observation of single-top-quark production with a W and Z boson at CMS

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: CMS reports the first observation of single-top-quark production in association with a W and Z boson in proton-proton collisions. A Particle Transformer classifier and improved reconstruction separated the rare tWZ signal from major backgrounds in three- and four-lepton events. Combining 13 and 13.6 TeV data (200 fb⁻¹), the measured signal has 5.8σ observed significance (3.5σ expected) and cross sections of 248 ± 52 fb at 13 TeV and 242 ± 77 fb at 13.6 TeV. The result agrees with the Standard Model within 2.3σ.

Technology: Particle Transformer (ParT) multiclass classifier

Editorial relevance 60 physics Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
CMS trained four ParT models, split by three- versus four-lepton signal region and 13 versus 13.6 TeV samples. In the three-lepton region, a four-node classifier distinguished tWZ, ttZ and other backgrounds; in the four-lepton region, a binary classifier separated tWZ from backgrounds. Its classifier-score categories entered the statistical signal extraction. The paper reports a substantial sensitivity gain versus the previous analysis: expected significance on the reused 13 TeV data rose from 1.4σ to 3.0σ, contributing to the first observation when combined with 13.6 TeV data.
Test and result
CMS reports the first observation of single-top-quark production in association with a W and Z boson in proton-proton collisions.
Limitation / still unknown
This is the first observation of the Standard-Model tWZ production process, not evidence for physics beyond the Standard Model. A 2024 CMS analysis had reported earlier evidence at 3.4σ; the 2026 paper adds 13.6 TeV Run 3 data and improved reconstruction/ML analysis to reach observation. The 5.8σ result combines 13 and 13.6 TeV datasets. Cross sections and signal strength are consistent with the Standard Model within the reported uncertainties.

11 Feb 2026Cedars-Sinai Medical Center; Valar Labs; Johns Hopkins University; University of Pittsburgh Medical Center; Pancreatic Cancer Action Network; University Health Network / Princess Margaret Cancer Centre

AI-derived histology biomarker stratifies first-line chemotherapy outcomes in advanced pancreatic cancer

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: The CHAI computational-histology platform generated a locked H&E-based biomarker intended to distinguish advanced pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma patients with differential outcomes on fluoropyrimidine-based versus gemcitabine-based chemotherapy. In an independent validation cohort of 299 patients from the prospectively collected COMPASS and Know Your Tumor cohorts, the 173 patients classified F-pref had longer time to next treatment or death (8.6 vs 7.5 months, P=.035) and overall survival (14.4 vs 11.7 months, P=.003) on F- versus G-based therapy. Among 126 G-pref patients, G-based therapy was associated with longer time to next treatment or death (9.6 vs 7.2 months, P=.038), but not significantly different overall survival.

Technology: Computational Histology Artificial Intelligence (CHAI) platform

Editorial relevance 53 medicine Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
Deep-learning models segmented H&E biopsy slides and quantified more than 30,000 histomorphologic features. Using the development cohort, the investigators statistically selected and weighted features into a treatment-preference biomarker and locked its threshold before applying it to an independent validation cohort. The platform supplied the image-derived feature measurements used in the biomarker; this is a biomarker-development and validation result, not autonomous treatment assignment.
Test and result
In an independent validation cohort of 299 patients from the prospectively collected COMPASS and Know Your Tumor cohorts, the 173 patients classified F-pref had longer time to next treatment or death (8.6 vs 7.5 months, P=.035) and overall survival (14.4 vs 11.7 months, P=.003) on F- versus G-based therapy. The locked biomarker was applied to assembled data from prospectively collected cohorts; prospective validation of treatment selection is still needed.
Limitation / still unknown
Validation used 299 patients in two prospectively collected but nonrandomized cohorts; treatment assignment was not randomized, and the authors also used propensity weighting and target-trial emulation. The primary endpoint was time to next treatment or death, not progression-free survival. In the biomarker’s G-pref subgroup, the OS comparison was not significant. The authors call for further prospective validation before clinical adoption. An earlier CHAI study concerned adjuvant gemcitabine outcomes in resected disease; this entry is limited to the distinct locked first-line fluoropyrimidine-versus-gemcitabine biomarker and external-cohort results in advanced disease.

AI contribution

AI contribution
A learned tract classifier identified language-pathway groups; conventional network measures and correlation analysis then related imaging changes to measured language changes.
Test and result
An 85-child preoperative tractography cohort supplied 47 training, 20 test and 18 later temporal-validation cases. Separate clinical analyses included 45 children with paired scans and 21 with paired scans/language assessments. CCA additionally fitted multivariate associations on these data.

The 21-child association is an exploratory within-study analysis, with multiple network/language comparisons and no stated independent CCA holdout. Cohort/scanner specificity, varying follow-up and incomplete outcome data limit generalization; surgical benefit, optimal margins and causal language effects were not established.

2 Jan 2026Standigm; and Ajou University School of Medicine

Knowledge-graph AI prioritizes TPP1 as a Parkinson’s disease target linked to α-synuclein homeostasis

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: Standigm ASK’s knowledge-graph model ranked Parkinson’s disease target associations; subgraph enrichment and expression analyses narrowed 2,527 predicted targets to five candidates, including TPP1. In a human cell-based α-synuclein seeding model, TPP1 knockdown increased aggregate accumulation and insoluble α-synuclein, experimentally supporting a TPP1–α-synuclein relationship and a possible protective role.

Technology: Standigm ASK knowledge-graph path-based deep-learning model with subgraph-level over-representation re-ranking

Editorial relevance 53 biology Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The model integrated heterogeneous biomedical databases, encoded relational paths using a convolutional network and attention aggregation, and produced disease-target scores. Researchers applied enrichment and transcriptomic filters to prioritize TPP1, then validated TPP1’s relationship to α-synuclein aggregation via siRNA knockdown and cellular assays; AlphaFold-Multimer modeling suggested, but did not prove, direct proteolysis.
Test and result
In a human cell-based α-synuclein seeding model, TPP1 knockdown increased aggregate accumulation and insoluble α-synuclein, experimentally supporting a TPP1–α-synuclein relationship and a possible protective role.
Limitation / still unknown
The functional experiment is a human neuroblastoma cell model exposed to α-synuclein preformed fibrils, not a clinical or in-vivo therapeutic demonstration. Knockdown increasing aggregation supports a protective association; direct enzymatic cleavage of α-synuclein is proposed from structural modeling, not established by the reported work. TPP1 is a candidate therapeutic target, not a validated treatment.
